inspirations.title: Inspirations
inspirations.intro: People and work that left fingerprints.

directors.title: Directors
directors.description: Framing, silence, rhythm and the courage to let a scene be strange.

items.label: Jiang Wen
items.note: Satire, cultural layering and the ability to make chaos feel completely deliberate.

items.label: Quentin Tarantino
items.note: Dialogue as violence; rhythm as narrative.

items.label: Stanley Kubrick
items.note: Precision, geometry and dread — every frame feels loaded.

items.label: Takeshi Kitano
items.note: Violence, stillness and poetic disconnection.

items.label: David Fincher
items.note: Cold, obsessive, surgical storytelling.

games.title: Games
games.description: Games that made atmosphere, systems or memory feel more important than spectacle.

items.label: Life Is Strange
items.note: Choices, mood and music — one of those games where everything emotionally clicks.

items.label: P.T
items.note: The scariest hallway ever made. Minimal space, maximum pressure.

items.label: Metal Gear
items.note: Story colliding with systems, politics and wonderfully unnecessary ideas.

items.label: Cyberpunk 2077
items.note: The city as a character; neon future as melancholy.

music.title: Artists
music.description: Artists whose sound keeps leaking into how I think about texture, space, rhythm and emotion.

items.label: Tame Impala
items.note: Psychedelic texture, bass lines and distortion that still knows how to groove.

items.label: JPEGMAFIA
items.note: Noise, glitches and ugly sounds arranged with ridiculous intention.

items.label: Mk.gee
items.note: Warped guitars, negative space and songs that feel half-broken but completely alive.

items.label: Porter Robinson
items.note: Electronic music with sincerity at its core. Nurture made vulnerability feel enormous.

items.label: Flume
items.note: Digital artefacts turned into musical texture.

items.label: Jack White
items.note: Raw electricity, compression and fuzz without sanding off the edges.

items.label: Radiohead
items.note: Anxiety, atmosphere and arrangement as architecture.

items.label: Dou Wei
items.note: From the claustrophobic rock of Black Dream to later ambient, experimental and improvisational work — always changing the language instead of repeating himself.

albums.title: 25 Albums That Stayed With Me
albums.description: 25 records that became part of me.

items.label: InnerSpeaker
items.note: Alive, imperfect, rough around the edges. Parts barely sound finished, and that’s why it’s my favourite album. No contest.

items.label: Kamikaze
items.note: It taught me to hit back after a setback. Also where I first started pulling rap apart: bars, punchlines, double meanings, the structure of the words.

items.label: Currents
items.note: Almost impossibly complete. Sound, melody, production, emotion. Everything lands exactly where it should.

items.label: good kid, m.A.A.d city
items.note: A documentary novel wearing hip-hop’s clothes. Growing up, family, the neighbourhood, violence, an era. One story that still sounds incredible and knows how to entertain.

items.label: 范特西
items.note: Jay Chou fully arriving at his own sound. R&B, hip-hop, Chinese influences, even some almost “garbage” MIDI. A flavour nothing else can replace.

items.label: SCARING THE HOES
items.note:
Complete loss of control, held tightly in place.

Two people smashing everything to pieces. Listen closer: every chaotic moment is ridiculously precise.

items.label: Nurture
items.note: Honest, fragile, almost defenceless. {{yearsSince2022}} years ago, at my lowest and nearly out of hope, this record helped me through.

items.label: 2014 Forest Hills Drive
items.note: Sincere. Someone who’s come a long way looking back at success, desire, family, growing up, and everything that got them here.

items.label: The Slim Shady LP
items.note:
My introduction to rap. Absurd, vicious, dark, childish, and stupidly funny.

The first time I realised words could be played with like this.

items.label: Lonerism
items.note:
I still remember my face on hearing the Endors Toi fuzz solo and that bouncy Apocalypse Dreams bass line for the first time. Pure joy.

Maybe not Tame Impala’s most perfect record. The one that made me love sound itself the most.

items.label: 黑梦
items.note: Cold, oppressive, distant, yet clear-headed. An empty city before dawn. Everything feels far away except your own consciousness.

items.label: My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy
items.note:
Baroque maximalism pushed almost as far as it can go.

Huge, lavish, narcissistic, chaotic. Everything thrown in, somehow still whole.

items.label: Nevermind
items.note:
Catchy, but heavy.

Instantly memorable melodies, with exhaustion, anger, boredom, and the feeling of imminent collapse underneath.

items.label: The Off-Season
items.note:
One of the 2020s’ closest things to a textbook classic rap album.

Little conceptual packaging. Just flow, writing, delivery, and beat selection pushed incredibly high.

items.label: UNLOCKED
items.note:
A car ride with two people who won’t say where you’re going. Strange, short, wonderful.

Every listen ends with: “Wait. That’s it?”

items.label: Carrie & Lowell
items.note:
Grief compressed until it barely moves.

No hysteria. Just memory, breathing, family, loss, and words you can’t say out loud.

items.label: IGOR
items.note:
A relationship moving through obsession, possession, jealousy, anger, and acceptance.

Its power isn’t in one song. You have to hear it all to live through the relationship.

items.label: Veteran
items.note:
It taught me that “abrasive”, “ugly”, and “beautiful” don’t cancel each other out.

Some sounds aren’t there to comfort you. They’re there to stay.

items.label: 新长征路上的摇滚
items.note:
The moment Chinese rock stood on its own feet, to me.

Raw, direct, unwilling to please. A new sound finding its own era.

items.label: Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band
items.note:
An album can be more than a dozen songs together.

It can be a whole world, with its own sound, logic, characters, and atmosphere.

items.label: 幻听
items.note:
Black Dream expressed emotion. Hallucination was already moving beyond the song.

Building space from sound: distant, open, free. Less and less like conventional pop.

items.label: 浮躁
items.note:
A pop album that barely tries to please anyone.

Light, cool, elusive, experimental, completely sure of itself. It owes nobody an explanation.

items.label: American Football
items.note:
A farewell to youth.

No grand goodbye. Just realising that people, places, and days you thought would never end have long been in the past.

items.label: Snow
items.note:
Quiet and light, like a winter morning.

Little drama. Just private, hard-to-name feelings that stay on your skin afterwards.

items.label: Music From Before the Storm
items.note:
One of the best game soundtracks ever, to me.

More than a score for Life is Strange: Before the Storm. The sound Chloe’s youth left behind.

encore.label: Ways To Get Out (Deluxe)
encore.note:
Some music stays because it fits your life.

Hazy, inward-looking, a little distant, always warm. Far Caspian never interrupts, yet stays beside you through ordinary days.

encore.label: F*CK U SKRILLEX YOU THINK UR ANDY WARHOL BUT UR NOT!! <3
encore.note:
Over a decade of hard-drive fragments, memories, noise, and unfinished thoughts emptied onto a table.

Fragmented, twitchy, absurdly messy. Sounds only Skrillex could make. A chaotic scrapbook of sound.

encore.label: Discovery
encore.note:
Electronic music can be romantic, warm, coloured by childhood fantasy.

The future, carrying a nostalgia you can’t return to. Somehow the machines made something deeply human.

foshoStory.eyebrow: A few notes from the workbench / 01
foshoStory.headline:
A face. A voice.
A place to begin.
foshoStory.context: FoSho · Made with the team at Metra
foshoStory.why: Experience fits on a CV. A voice, a manner, a bit of personality need a little more room. FoSho starts with a short video introduction, giving people another way to be understood.
foshoStory.audience: Built around casual, part-time, volunteer and early-career opportunities. Job seekers can introduce themselves; employers can share an opportunity and get a better sense of the person behind an application.
foshoStory.flowIntro: Three moments in the product. Enough room to prepare, and a clear choice about what happens next.
foshoStory.flowCaption: A sketch of the documented product flow.

steps.label: Say hello
steps.title: A short introduction.
steps.body: Record with the camera, or bring a video already made. Framing controls and a teleprompter help with the awkward part: finding a comfortable way to begin.

steps.label: Make it yours
steps.title: Preview before publishing.
steps.body: Trim, reframe, zoom or mirror the preview. Add the details that help people find it, then publish. The editing preview keeps the original source file intact.
steps.detail: A little room to get it right.

steps.label: Start talking
steps.title: A conversation by invitation.
steps.body: Explore people and opportunities, then send a message request. The recipient accepts before the full conversation opens. A small step that keeps the inbox in their hands.

decisions.title: Keep the original.
decisions.body: The editing flow separates a preview from the source video. Trying a different crop or trim should leave room to change your mind.

decisions.title: Let people set the pace.
decisions.body: Message requests put acceptance before a conversation. Discovery opens a door; it does not need to remove the handle.

decisions.title: Comfort belongs in the product.
decisions.body: Theme, contrast, text size, motion and image visibility can be adjusted. These preferences stay with the user across visits.

foshoStory.role: Frontend lead · Backend collaborator · Project manager
foshoStory.contribution: Leading the product direction for Metra and FoSho, shaping the platform structure, and designing and building the main frontend experience. Working across the backend where product decisions need to become dependable system behaviour, while keeping the project moving as a team.
foshoStory.technicalTitle: A little further under the hood
foshoStory.technical: React and TypeScript on the web; Expo and React Native on mobile. A Spring Boot backend connects PostgreSQL, video processing with FFmpeg, and media delivery through S3 and CloudFront.
foshoStory.validation: The project documentation records frontend typecheck, lint and build checks, mobile typechecking, and backend compile and test stages. Camera permissions, editing, messaging and accessibility settings also need hands-on review.
foshoStory.closing: FoSho is temporarily offline. The work, the decisions and the lessons still belong here.
